summary: Target-level plan for all eight stages. PG imports from PadicHodgeTheory (P7 interfaces and P8 relative period sheaves) and FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory the cyclotomic coefficients, Fontaine's equivalence, overconvergence, field-coefficient Herr cohomology and the Wach–D_cris comparison, which those lower-tier roadmaps now own. It plans the extended-ring, integral and relative extensions, the φ–ψ comparison and ψ operator, the derived Iwasawa comparison, Wach good bases and Iwasawa classes, and the Kedlaya–Pottharst–Xiao relative cohomology, rank-one classification and global triangulation.

conventions.scalar: Use two copies R and S and the specified Frobenius algebra map. Do not let an inferred identity self-algebra change the tensor product or trace. Normalized trace is constructed integrally at its scalar owner before p-torsion reduction; trace=0 modulo p does not define psi.
conventions.fixedCoefficients: Herr operators and kernels are linear over a fixed coefficient ring C. Phi/psi need not be linear over the period ring. An algebraic basis does not automatically give continuous coordinates in every weak/annular topology.
conventions.torsion: KPX Delta_K is the p-torsion subgroup, trivial for odd p. The roadmap odd-prime full prime-to-p torsion convention requires a comparison; it is not silently identified with KPX. Rational order-two averaging and integral p=2 derived descent are different.
conventions.signs: d0=((F-1),(G-1)), d1=((G-1),-(F-1)); signed comparison=(id,diag(-psi,id),-psi). The psi complex is in cohomological degrees 1 and 2.
conventions.comparison: F:C_phi→C_psi, S:C_psi→C_phi. In functional notation FS=id and id-SF=dH+Hd. In categorical notation S followed by F is identity, and the homotopy is between id and F followed by S.
conventions.status: Target-level planning pass complete under PROTOCOL §0; every stage planned and none closed. Nine nodes are comparison receipts for lower-tier owners and twelve are narrowed to what PG adds (restructure entry 1). No formalisation claim. The compact suggested Lean file elaborates at the pins with only admitted-proof warnings.
conventions.radius: KPX φ maps [s,r] to [s/p,r/p]; Berger’s r parameter grows when the inner geometric radius approaches 1. Never identify these numerical parameters without an adapter.
conventions.weights: HT(Q_p(1))=+1. Berger-positive means all weights ≤0. For [a,b], use T(−b), then N(T)=π^{-b}N(T(−b)) with its Tate basis.
conventions.components: Main notation uses a connected coefficient ring and Γ_K. KL’s all-component Γ=Z_p^× category is compared by induction/restriction, not identified by notation.
conventions.families: Relative modules are finite projective. No universal freeness, global étale lattice, crystalline period rank or underived specialization is inferred from fibres.

nodes.title: Semilinear Frobenius modules
nodes.statement: For a commutative ring S with endomorphism σ, a Frobenius module consists of an S-module M and an S-linear isomorphism S⊗_{S,σ}M → M. Its associated map F(m)=L(1⊗m) is σ-semilinear. Morphisms are S-linear maps commuting with F. Finite generation, projectivity and freeness are separate conditions.
hypotheses: S commutative; σ:S→S unital; no invertibility of σ assumed.
proofSteps: Use the existing tensor product with right S-action through σ.
Recover L from a semilinear F by the tensor universal property; require that this L is invertible.
Composition and identities are those of underlying linear maps.
acceptance: Do not replace invertible linearization by a bijective underlying F; those differ when σ is not surjective.

sources.match: Defines semilinear Frobenius through an invertible twisted tensor linearization, with distinct finite/projective/free variants.

nodes.title: Free Frobenius covers and projective complements
nodes.statement: Every finitely generated Frobenius module is a quotient of a finite free Frobenius module. For finite projective M, the kernel N of such a cover is finite projective and the underlying S-module M⊕N is finite free; no equivariant splitting of the quotient is asserted.
hypotheses: The Frobenius action is an invertible linearization; M finitely generated; projectivity is added only for the complement assertion.
proofSteps: Choose generators of M and matrices describing the linearization and its inverse.
Enlarge the generator set using the defect matrix; the block matrix is invertible by clearing its top-left block.
For projective M split the surjection S-linearly and give its kernel the induced Frobenius action.
acceptance: A splitting of underlying modules need not commute with Frobenius; keep that distinction in all complement arguments.

nodes.title: Frobenius cohomology as Ext
nodes.statement: The complex [M --(F−1)→ M] in degrees 0 and 1 computes Ext^i_{S{F}}(S,M); its cohomology is the kernel in degree 0, cokernel in degree 1 and zero in higher degrees.
hypotheses: S{F} is the skew polynomial ring with F s=σ(s)F; S is its left module via σ; M is a left skew-ring module.
proofSteps: Use the two-term free left S{F}-resolution of S whose differential is right multiplication by F−1.
Compare its Hom complex to the displayed additive differential; the latter is generally not S-linear.
For F^d use cyclic induction, retaining the enlarged scalar fixed ring.
acceptance: Use additive or fixed-scalar cochains: F−1 is not an S-linear map for arbitrary σ.

nodes.statement: The étale condition over B_K, B_K^† and the Robba ring R_K, with finite coefficients, is the owner's (PadicHodgeTheory:P7/phi-gamma-module-interface): a lattice over A_K or A_K^† with invertible Frobenius linearization, and over R_K descent to such an overconvergent module, equivalently all Newton slopes zero. This node adds the two variants PG.1–PG.2 use. (i) Over the integral rings A_K and A_K^†, an étale (φ,Γ_K)-module is a finite projective module with invertible Frobenius linearization and a continuous semilinear Γ_K-action commuting with φ. (ii) Over the extended rings B̃_K, B̃_K^† and R̃_K, a (φ,Γ_K)-module is étale when its underlying φ-module descends to a φ-module over Ã_K, Ã_K^† and Ã_K^† respectively. In each case the property does not depend on the chosen descent, and Γ_K acts on some descent but not necessarily on every one.
hypotheses: Integral lattice spans the rational module; Γ-stable lattices are chosen when transporting integral representations.
For a relative affinoid, global lattice existence is additional data and is not deduced from pointwise conditions.

Prove that compatible scalar extensions preserve the property and formulate morphisms without fixing a descent.

nodes.title: Analytic inverse on ψ-zero modules
nodes.statement: For a finite projective (φ,Γ_K)-module M over the relative Robba ring with Q_p-affinoid coefficients A, and a topological generator γ of Γ_K/Δ_K, γ−1 is invertible on M^{ψ=0}. At every sufficiently small admissible radius, the ψ-zero module carries the compatible analytic group-ring structure and is finite projective of rank [K:Q_p]rank(M). The retained signed φ-to-ψ comparison therefore is a quasi-isomorphism in this rational setting.
hypotheses: Use the analytic group ring at the radius appearing in KPX Theorem 3.1.1; the full Robba assertion is obtained by compatible gluing.
This theorem asserts no integral-lattice preservation of the inverse.
proofSteps: Reduce by induction to Q_p. On a sufficiently small annulus decompose ψ-zero vectors into unit-index Frobenius cosets.
Choose a small Γ power for which ||γ_n−1|| is bounded below the annular parameter norm. Invert G=(1+π)γ_n−1 by factoring out π and summing the resulting convergent Neumann series.
Choose a projective complement making the underlying module free; extend the auxiliary operator by π on the complement, without asserting an equivariant splitting.
Use the near-identity substitution and uniform finite generation to obtain finite projectivity over the analytic group ring, pass between Γ powers and glue the radius-compatible inverses.
Restrict to the torsion-invariant summand and apply the algebraic signed comparison.
acceptance: The proof must converge in the annular seminorms actually used; a formal geometric series is insufficient.

nodes.title: Derived integral Iwasawa comparison
nodes.statement: For a finite free O_E-representation T of G_K, compare the independent inverse-corestriction complex Rlim_n RΓ_cont(K_n,T) to [D(T) --(ψ−1)→D(T)] in degrees 1 and 2 as a complex of continuous Λ_{O_E}(Γ_K)-modules. Establish the comparison before deducing H¹_Iw≅D(T)^{ψ=1} and H²_Iw≅coker(ψ−1). Finite O_E-torsion variants use the integral descent theorem, not rational division of trace. At p=2 use PG.3’s derived torsion descent.
hypotheses: K finite over Q_p; E finite over Q_p with ring O_E; K_n a fixed cofinal cyclotomic tower; continuous and derived inverse limits are the supplier’s objects.
The concrete integral comparison proof and inverse-limit hypotheses remain named gaps.
proofSteps: Compare each finite-layer continuous complex with its integral period resolution and identify corestriction with the normalized trace transition. The degree-one isomorphism D(T)^{ψ=1}≅H¹_Iw is Cherbonnier–Colmez 1999, Théorème II.1.3 (after Fontaine); the cochain-level comparison and the degree-two term are the targets here.
Construct the compatible inverse-system comparison at cochain level; the Γ action is the actual tower action.
Compute its derived inverse limit, retaining H⁰ and lim¹ terms until their vanishing or cancellation is proved.
Identify the resulting fibre with ψ−1 in the specified shift and prove naturality; only then apply the retained native homology isomorphisms.

The absence of a degree-zero term in the ψ complex is a comparison theorem, not an argument that all inverse-limit corrections vanish.

nodes.title: Iwasawa field maps, twists and coefficients
nodes.statement: The derived Iwasawa–ψ comparison commutes with maps of lattices, finite extension L/K and corestriction, finite-flat coefficient extension and Tate twisting. The rational object is (Rlim_n RΓ(K_n,T))⊗^L_{O_E}E; it is compared with the rational ψ model through this order, without identifying it with an arbitrary inverse limit of rational cochains.

The comparison preserves the finite-layer integration/corestriction normalization. Ordinary specialization of H^i requires vanishing of the adjoining Tor term; otherwise retain the derived base-change spectral sequence.

nodes.title: Analytic Iwasawa comparison and generation after Robba scalar extension
nodes.statement: For a finite-dimensional E-representation V of G_K, analytic extension of classical rational Iwasawa cohomology identifies with H^i(C_ψ(D_rig(V))) as in KPX Theorem 4.4.11; rationalization is after the integral inverse limit. For the generation assertion of Proposition 4.3.8, take K=Q_p, A=E, M a Robba (φ,Γ)-module and M*=M∨(1), and assume M/(ψ−1)=M*/(ψ−1)=0. Then φ−1 is injective on M^{ψ=1}, the Iwasawa pairing is perfect, and, for an admissible r₀, C⊗_{R_E^∞(Γ)}R_E^{r₀}(Γ)≅(M^{r₀})^{ψ=0}, where C=(φ−1)M^{ψ=1}. Here R_E^∞(Γ) is the distribution algebra and R_E^{r₀}(Γ) is the larger Robba-type Γ ring. No generation over distributions alone follows.
hypotheses: E finite over Q_p; the first comparison allows finite K/Q_p. The generation clause is the stated K=Q_p field case and requires both ψ cokernels to vanish.
Admissible radius, analytic group-ring topology and coadmissible scalar extension are supplied by LocallyAnalyticDistributions.
proofSteps: Compare the classical tower through compact induction, Shapiro and the ψ-complex; rationalize after the inverse limit.
Apply the derived cyclotomic deformation comparison for the analytic extension.
Under both vanishing hypotheses use Iwasawa duality to prove perfectness; compare the two finite free modules of the same rank after extension to R_E^{r₀}(Γ), as in Proposition 4.3.8.

For a Dospinescu–Le Bras consumer retain the separate obligations to verify these hypotheses on tN_rig(V), extend the involution through (γ−1)^{-1}, and control its radius. The paper does not verify them.

nodes.title: Wach modules with a weight interval
nodes.statement: Let F/Q_p be finite unramified and q=φ(π)/π. For weights in [a,b], a Wach lattice N is finite free over A_F^+ (or the E-coefficient analogue), with continuous semilinear Γ_F action trivial on N/πN, and a semilinear map φ:N[1/π]→N[1/φ(π)] commuting with Γ_F such that φ(π^bN)⊂π^bN and the linearized quotient of π^bN by φ^*(π^bN) is killed by q^{b−a}. For the rational version over B_F^+, where p is a unit, also require that B_F⊗_{B_F^+}N is an étale (φ,Γ_F)-module (Berger's 2026 erratum to Definition III.4.1; source issue E2); for an integral lattice over A_F^+ this holds because q is a unit in A_F. Require the prescribed embedding into the étale period module when N is attached to a representation. Use HT(Q_p(1))=+1 throughout.
hypotheses: F is unramified; a≤b integers; rational N(V) uses B_F^+, integral N(T) uses A_F^+.
Frobenius changes the localization from π to φ(π)=qπ; it is not generally an endomorphism of N[1/π], since q need not be a unit there.
proofSteps: Use finite free modules and commuting semilinear actions on the positive period ring.
Impose trivial residual Γ action and the q-power linearized height condition after the indicated weight shift.
Define morphisms by intertwining the actions; keep the embedding in D(T) as comparison data.
acceptance: Do not strengthen the height condition to invertibility of φ^*N→N; nonzero weights can have nonzero height.
Record both localization rings in the Frobenius map; do not invert q without an explicit scalar extension.
Without the étaleness of B_F⊗N the rational definition does not force N to come from a representation (source issue E2).

nodes.title: Crystalline Wach existence and uniqueness
nodes.statement: For a crystalline Q_p-representation V of G_F, F/Q_p finite unramified, and a G_F-stable Z_p-lattice T, there is a unique Wach module N(T)⊂D(T) with the stated weight interval, spanning D(T) after the prescribed period extension. For positive V, with all weights ≤0, it lies in D^+(T) and contains π^rD^+(T) when weights lie in [−r,0]. Its rationalization is N(V), and arbitrary intervals are obtained by the fixed Tate twist.
hypotheses: V crystalline, F unramified, T finite free; coefficient E variants use commuting finite coefficient action.
No arbitrary ramified-field, merely de Rham, or pointwise crystalline family version is asserted.
proofSteps: Use finite-height crystalline descent to choose a positive lattice and kill the residual Γ action.
Prove saturation by the distinguished q_n factors; use the residual O_F-module and lifting to prove freeness, rather than treating A_F^+ as a PID.
Prove uniqueness by comparing the lowest π-power of two candidate lattices and the nontrivial χ-power on its quotient.
Intersect the rational Wach object with the étale lattice to recover N(T); twist for arbitrary [a,b].
acceptance: Finite height alone is not equated with crystallinity; the Γ-trivial residual condition and source hypotheses remain essential.

The integral comparison π^r(A^+⊗T)⊂A^+⊗N(T) gives the required bounded lattice control. General intervals use the fixed twist.

Transport the resulting inequalities under the explicit interval twist.

nodes.title: Wach reconstruction and allowed operations
nodes.statement: Rational Wach modules are equivalent to crystalline representations over unramified F, compatibly with tensor products, duals and exact sequences. For each crystalline V, G_F-stable lattices in V correspond inclusion-preservingly to integral Wach lattices in N(V). Recover T from the étale φ-fixed construction after extending the Wach lattice to its étale period module. The integral correspondence is not asserted to preserve every short exact sequence or arbitrary quotient.
hypotheses: Source weight-interval conditions and finite freeness; exactness is claimed for the rational equivalence.
proofSteps: Extend the Wach lattice to an étale module and recover the representation through the already constructed inverse functor.
Use Wach uniqueness to identify both comparison maps, and to compare tensor and dual lattices after rationalization.
Compare intersections with D(T) to prove the lattice inclusion correspondence; leave nonsaturated integral quotients outside the exactness claim.

nodes.statement: For finite unramified F′/F, the Wach module of T|G_F′ is A_F′^+⊗_{A_F^+}N_F(T), with the canonical descent comparison. Finite flat extension of integral coefficient rings commutes with Wach formation; rational coefficient change commutes with N(V), D_cris and their filtered comparison. These maps respect interval twists and compose along towers.
hypotheses: Both local base fields unramified over Q_p; the integral coefficient map is finite flat; weights are those of a crystalline representation, not only pointwise family data.
proofSteps: Use the imported unramified ring extension and the Witt Frobenius on its coefficients.
Check freeness, Γ reduction and q-height after flat extension; uniqueness identifies the result with the new Wach module.
Prove the composition cocycle by the same uniqueness and compare the filtered period maps.

nodes.title: Good Wach bases for the regulator interface
nodes.statement: For crystalline V over Q_p with coefficients E, choose the LLZ source-normalized Wach model. Given a basis ν_i of D_cris(V), there exists a B^+_{Q_p}⊗E-basis n_i of N(V) lifting ν_i such that (1+π)φ(n_i) is a Λ_E(Γ)-basis of (φ^*N(V))^{ψ=0}; the analytic scalar extension is an H_E(Γ)-basis. Under the integral hypotheses of LLZ §3A there exists an integral good basis. Export the chosen basis and its linear coordinate isomorphism; Coleman maps and their images belong to the regulator roadmap.
hypotheses: E/Q_p is finite and V is crystalline over Q_p; N(V) uses the Tate-twist normalization of LLZ §1C4. The rational basis statement is Theorem 2.12, independent of the noncritical refinement used for the preceding elementary-divisor theorem.

For the integral §3A interface, all Hodge–Tate weights are nonnegative, V has no trivial quotient, and T is a G_Qp-stable O_E-lattice. Existence of an integral good basis does not prescribe its reduction or make every basis good.
proofSteps: The source recalls rational good-basis existence from LLZ 2010, Lemma 3.15, and integral existence from its Theorem 3.5. Their original proofs remain a recorded gap; do not present the 2011 recall as a proof.
Compare bounded and analytic bases by the closedness/density argument of Proposition 2.11.
Construct the coordinate isomorphism and state its transformation under two selected good bases using their actual Λ-linear coordinate change.
acceptance: LLZ Remark 2.14 calls the arbitrary-basis assertion a conjecture; no such assertion is exported.
The Wach φ matrix changes by B^{-1}Pφ(B) for column-coordinate convention; the induced analytic coordinate change must be proved, not obtained by replacing φ(B) with B.

A relative (φ,Γ_K)-module is a finite projective module with invertible φ-linearization and continuous semilinear Γ_K-action commuting with φ; use radius models and their canonical restrictions. Define M[1/t] by localization. Morphisms, tensor, dual and determinant use the existing module operations. For an Artinian coefficient algebra retain the stable-lattice condition used by BHS for the localized subcategory.

nodes.title: Saturated triangulations and strict parameters

nodes.statement: Use the character-space weight coordinates supplied by L0a, with the following interpretation for the PG rank-one and Sen interfaces. An algebraic character is ∏_σ x_σ^{k_σ} with fixed integers k_σ; a constant character takes values in E^×; a smooth character has all weights zero; a locally algebraic character is a product of a smooth and an algebraic character.
